author: codex

patch.value: Atomic aggregate failure receipt overstates rollback certainty

Greptile review of PR 73 found that the aggregate atomic-import catch claimed every create was compensated and no committed items remained. That is stronger than the implementation: create cleanup is best-effort and deliberately tolerates an unavailable status lookup or failed close so the remaining sweep can continue, while update compensation is intentionally a no-op pending pm-csv-71zg. Replace the false clean-state assertion with an explicit reconciliation warning that names the transaction and both limitations.

A red regression rejects the old rolled-back and clean-tracker assertion; Every aggregate atomic failure names the transaction and says mutations may remain; The receipt explicitly identifies best-effort create cleanup and intentionally non-reverted pre-existing updates; The receipt directs the operator to inspect and reconcile before retrying; Exact all-source coverage and all release gates remain green
Run an atomic keyed import whose first row updates an existing item and whose later row fails; inspect the aggregate CommandError.
Atomic failure output never claims a clean tracker unless the implementation has actually verified every mutation was reverted.
The exact-head error asserted complete rollback even when compensation could be incomplete or updates intentionally remained.

message: Implement truthful aggregate atomic failure receipt
